subject: ela
intro: Fifth graders adapt their speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, using formal English (complete sentences, standard grammar, polite words) in formal situations like presentations, and informal English with friends. They choose the right register for the audience and purpose.

items.prompt: You are giving a formal presentation. Which is more appropriate: 'Okay guys, so like, here's the deal' or 'Good afternoon. Today I will present my findings on renewable energy'?

steps: A formal presentation calls for formal English.
'Good afternoon. Today I will present...' is formal and complete.
solution.answer: 'Good afternoon. Today I will present my findings on renewable energy.'

items.prompt: You are chatting with friends at lunch. Which fits: 'What's up? Wanna sit here?' or 'Greetings. May I request to join your table?'

steps: Chatting with friends is an informal context.
'What's up? Wanna sit here?' fits the casual setting.
So that fits the informal context.

items.prompt: In a speech to the school board, you should use ____ English.

steps: Speaking to an official group is formal.

items.prompt: Talking with friends can use ____ English.
Match your speech to the ____ and purpose.
